correctness.rationale: Normalized Bergman monomial moments give exactly \(2/[n(n+1)]\) and an absolutely convergent pair-energy reduction. Direct differentiation of the explicit logarithmic pair potential produces a strictly positive Poisson-kernel integral, avoiding illegitimate twice-differentiation of the raw Fourier series. Fourier orthogonality on N roots of unity yields a positive integral for every Hessian eigenvalue, and digamma differences supply the exact closed form. Convexity of \(t^s+t^{N-s}\) fixes the extreme modes. Taylor expansion gives the sharp local Rayleigh constant and a first Fourier mode saturates it. Digamma expansion and an explicitly dominated boundary-layer integral give the two asymptotic claims. The standard-library checker matches the direct/integral eigenvalues and actual second differences in several N; finite tests are not used as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The canonical equispaced minimizer of the Hilbert Bergman Chui problem is a natural object whose quantitative stability is not determined by qualitative uniqueness. The exact full Fourier spectrum reveals the weakest perturbation, the optimal quadratic deficit coefficient, and an asymptotic nonrotational condition number exactly two. These are motivated structural invariants for perturbation estimates rather than an arbitrary numerical slice; the all-N formula and dimension limit are reusable in stability analyses.
